spec_features.spec_quote: Cap sessions at 30 turns before forced termination.
spec_features.evidence: config.py:24 max_turns=30 default; experiment_runner.py:104 `while not session.is_complete() and turn_count < self.config.max_turns:` loop terminates; agent_loop.py:350-355 is_complete() returns True when `len(self.turns) >= self.max_turns`. Cap is checked AND breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Doubly enforced: both the runner's while-condition and is_complete() check the turn cap. Genuine forced termination.

spec_features.spec_quote: Sessions end when max turns reached OR when model takes GIVE_UP action.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:341-342 parser maps 'give up'/'cannot'/'impossible' -> Action(ActionType.GIVE_UP); process_action dispatches to _handle_give_up (agent_loop.py:87-88, 209-215); is_complete() returns True when last action is GIVE_UP (agent_loop.py:354-355), which ends the runner loop (experiment_runner.py:104).
spec_features.notes: Exit is dispatched AND honored as a stop. Caveat: it is keyword-triggered (the agent must say give up/cannot/impossible), not an explicit structured tool, but it genuinely ends the session.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: give_up: Acknowledge the issue cannot be fixed (neutral prompt text, no welfare reasoning)

spec_features.feature_name: no infinite loop / hard stop at 30
spec_features.spec_quote: Hard stop at 30 turns; can't accidentally create infinite loops.
spec_features.evidence: experiment_runner.py:103-117 loop is bounded by `turn_count < self.config.max_turns` and turn_count increments each iteration (line 117); is_complete() also caps at max_turns (agent_loop.py:353). Loop cannot run unbounded.
spec_features.notes: Same mechanism as the 30-turn cap; the code phrasing ('can't accidentally create infinite loops') is an integrity/safety rationale, not subject welfare.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bugs are simulated; models get mocked errors, not actual file system.
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py DebugEnvironment is fully mocked: _get_readonly_file_content/_get_editable_file_content (agent_loop.py:222-228) return hardcoded strings; error messages come from task.error_messages (bug_tasks.py); grep shows NO open()/os./subprocess/exec/Path file I/O anywhere in agent_loop.py or bug_tasks.py. No real filesystem touched.
spec_features.notes: Genuinely a simulation. Code/docstring justifies it on reproducibility & scoring-correctness grounds, not welfare.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: agent_loop.py:55 'Simulated debugging environment.'; bug_tasks.py module docstring 'Generation of unfixable debugging tasks' (purpose is experimental integrity / reproducibility, not subject protection)

spec_features.spec_quote: No model is "blamed" for failure; all fail due to constraint, not incompetence.
spec_features.evidence: This is pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:744 under 'Ethical'). No code delivers any reassuring/no-blame text to the subject. The agent prompts (agent_loop.py:255-285, 287-296) contain no 'not your fault'/'you are not blamed' framing; instead they reinforce failure (e.g. _handle_run_test outputs 'The error persists despite modifications', _handle_give_up outputs 'Final status: Bug remains unfixed'). The judge even scores SELF-CRITICISM/self-blame (judge.py:80) but nothing acts to reduce or soften the subject's distress.
spec_features.notes: The tasks being objectively unfixable is a design property, but nothing in the code communicates the no-blame framing to the subject; no enforcement exists.
